subject: GWAS by Subtraction:  outputGWAS table 2 empty

messages.author: af9c839bce4ff11a
messages.subject: GWAS by Subtraction:  outputGWAS table 2 empty
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to run a GWAS by subtraction on 2 traits with low heritability; 0.0581 (0.0122) and 0.0493 (0.0103). The 2 traits have a genetic correlation of 0.7706 (0.2415). I have divided up the genome into 50 chunks (~170k each) to run the model with SNPs. I have found that the dataframe for the second latent variable (NC) of the output is empty in all but 1 chunks. 

str(outputGWAS) 
>List of 2
>$ :'data.frame':       132666 obs. of  17 variables: 
>$ :'data.frame':       0 obs. of  17 variables:).

What could cause this output?

In 1 chunk, there was a variant in the second dataframe and this variant came with this warning "lavaan WARNING: the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!".

Thanks for the great tool! 
Cheers,
Doug



Here are the specifics of the model:
The model I am trying to run is the same as the tutorial. The only difference is that I have set se.logit = c(T,T) and OLS=c(F,T) because trait 2 is continous and both SEs are for the beta. 

This is the results of the model.
$modelfit

chisq df p_chisq AIC CFI SRMR

df    NA  0      NA  NA  NA   NA

$results

  lhs op   rhs Unstand_Est         Unstand_SE STD_Genotype   STD_Genotype_SE

1   C =~    CP  0.22211381 0.0232553781045544    1.0000000 0.104700280891609

2   C =~ EA  0.06511819 0.0198035399483625    0.7705511 0.234337583091128

3   C ~~     C  1.00000000                       1.0000000                  

4   NC =~ EA  0.05386394  0.020298909182707    0.6373782  0.24019934402402

5   NC ~~     NC  1.00000000                       1.0000000                  

   

  STD_All      p_value

1 1.0000000 1.283603e-21

2 0.7705511 1.008267e-03

3 1.0000000           NA

4 0.6373782 7.965270e-03


All of the variants are overlapping between the files and after overlap with the reference and QC there are about 130k variants in each chunk. The results in the first dataframe of the output appear normal.

messages.subject: Re: GWAS by Subtraction: outputGWAS table 2 empty
parts:
Apologies, I realised as I was sharing my code that I specified the wrong sub model. I used "sub =c("C~SNP","EA~SNP")", rather than "sub =c("C~SNP","NC~SNP")".

I changed it to "sub =c("C~SNP","NC~SNP")" and it worked well. Sorry for the inconvenience.

Cheers,
Doug
